prompt: Derive the relation P = Fv from the definitions of power and work done, where P is the power developed by a constant force F acting on a body moving with constant velocity v in the direction of the force.

mark_scheme.criterion: States P = W / t and substitutes work done W = Fs to give P = Fs / t (or P = F(s / t)).
States v = s / t and concludes with P = Fv.

hints: Start with the definition of power: P = W / t.
Substitute W = Fs and use velocity v = s / t.
solution: Power is defined as work done per unit time: P = W / t. Work done by a constant force is W = Fs, where s is displacement in the direction of the force. Substituting gives P = Fs / t = F(s / t). Since velocity v = s / t, this yields P = Fv.
teacher_walkthrough: Award C1 for writing P = W / t and W = Fs to form P = F(s / t).
Award A1 for recognizing v = s / t to achieve P = Fv.
